title: RX_TIMEOUT_MS of 5000ms may starve other work
description:
lora_l2.c:42: #define RX_TIMEOUT_MS 5000

The RX thread blocks in lora_recv for up to 5 seconds per iteration. During this time, the running flag is not checked (it's only checked at loop top).

What goes wrong: lichen_lora_l2_stop() sets running=0 and joins the thread. If the thread is blocked in lora_recv, stop waits up to 5.1 seconds (100ms + 5000ms join timeouts).

This is documented and handled (abort after timeout), but 5 seconds is long for a stop operation. A user calling disable/enable in quick succession may see unexpected delays.

Fix: Consider shorter RX timeout (500-1000ms) with the understanding that more loop iterations means more running-flag checks. Or expose via Kconfig. The current 5s is reasonable for battery savings but poor for responsiveness.
close_reason: Already fixed in current HEAD by a prior review-fix wave; verified, no further change needed. The bead's 'or expose via Kconfig' option was implemented: lora_l2.c:153 now uses #define RX_TIMEOUT_MS CONFIG_LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS, and firmware/bridge-zephyr/subsys/lichen/Kconfig:122-137 adds config LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS with default 1000 (inside the bead's recommended 500-1000ms band, down from the reviewed hard-coded 5000), range 100-10000, and help text documenting the responsiveness/power trade-off. Stop-latency interaction (100ms quick join + timeout budget) documented in lichen_lora_l2_stop(). Verified: clang -fsyntax-only -std=c11 -Wall --target=armv7m-none-eabi on lora_l2.c with stub Zephyr headers and Kconfig-default -D flags (incl. -DCONFIG_LICHEN_LORA_L2_RX_TIMEOUT_MS=1000): exit 0 (1 stub-artifact warning: 'state_names not needed' - artifact of stub LOG macros discarding args, not a code issue). CI gap: native_sim / pinned Zephyr v3.7.0 build not runnable locally.
